newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pilots' stike hits Air France Europe flights.
newsitem.headline: Pilots' stike hits Air France Europe flights.

text.p: A snap one-day strike by pilots at Air France Europe, the domestic wing of Air France, disrupted flights on Thursday in a union protest at plans to restructure the airline and cut wages.

"We're maintaining 60 percent of all flights," a spokeswoman said. She said the strike was not as crippling as some previous stoppages because the biggest pilots' union, the SNPL, was not taking part.

Pilots are protesting at a new system to lease planes from other carriers and a plan announced last year to merge Air France Europe, formerly Air Inter, into the main international airline of Air France.

When the strike was called on Wednesday, the company had expected to guarantee only a third of flights on major routes, between Paris and Marseille, Toulouse and Strasbourg as well as flights to Corsica.
It had expected to cancel all others but had vowed not to give in to what it called "blackmail" from the best paid pilots in the world, staging a 41st strike in two years.
The three striking unions, the USPNT, SNPNAC and SPIT, accused Air France Chairman Christian Blanc in a statement of "hooligan methods" and of choosing confrontation rather than negotiation.

The reforms would cut some money-losing routes and lower Air France Europe pilots' salaries by about 15 percent to bring them into line with Air France. The unions last went on strike for a day on February 9.
